summary: kepler dependency-confusion lure resolves install-script package from non-registry host
details: kepler@2.999.999 is a near-empty package whose package.json declares a single dependency `flag-serial-object-syntax` pinned to the hardcoded URL `https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/flag-serial-object-syntax` instead of an npm registry name. The shrinkwrap records `hasInstallScript: true` for that dependency, so `npm install kepler` fetches an arbitrary tarball from artifacts.yosiroute.com and runs its lifecycle scripts on the installer's machine. The advertised version 2.999.999 conflicts with the README and index.js which describe version 1.0.0; the 999-inflated semver is the canonical dependency-confusion pattern used to win resolution against an internal/private package of the same name. The package provides no functional library code — its only install-time effect is dropping and executing code from a non-registry host outside npm.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
